items.headline: Solid-state battery maker Factorial to go public through SPAC merger
items.summary: A merger with a blank-check company is one way for a solid-state battery startup to raise growth capital.

items.headline: Tulip Innovation wins German injunctions against Sunwoda over separator patents
items.summary: Shows that battery separator patents can lead to German sales injunctions, which matters for anyone selling cells into the EU.

items.headline: LG Energy Solution wins German battery patent lawsuit against Sunwoda
items.summary: Major Korean cell makers are enforcing their patents in Europe, which affects how startups plan supply chains and freedom-to-operate checks.

items.headline: Ninth Circuit sends instrument repairer's antitrust suit against Intuitive back to trial court
items.summary: This antitrust case, not a patent case, could affect whether third parties can service or remanufacture da Vinci instruments.

items.headline: J&J MedTech's OTTAVA robot gets FDA de novo classification
items.summary: Another major company now has an FDA-authorized surgical robot, adding competition and another possible partner or acquirer for startups.

items.headline: CMR Surgical wins FDA clearance for upgraded Versius Plus robot
items.summary: Getting FDA clearance for an upgrade after a first clearance shows a step-by-step regulatory path new surgical-robot makers can follow.

items.headline: Solventum agrees to acquire privately held Acera Surgical
items.summary: A large medtech company buying a privately held surgical bioscience company shows that acquisition is a realistic exit for startups in this field.

items.headline: Federal Circuit upholds cutting Rex Medical's $10M award against Intuitive to nominal damages
items.summary: A patent holder can win on infringement and still recover almost nothing if its damages evidence doesn't isolate the patent's value, which affects how much a surgical-tool patent is worth to assert or license.
items.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit

items.headline: Patent office rules challengers must argue the same claim meaning as in court
items.summary: Anyone challenging a drug patent at the patent office, or defending one, must now argue the same claim meaning there as in parallel court cases.

items.headline: Merck closes $10B acquisition of Verona Pharma, maker of COPD drug Ohtuvayre
items.summary: Shows big pharma will pay heavily for a single first-in-class drug in a common disease like COPD.

items.headline: FormFactor acquires Keystone Photonics, silicon photonics wafer-probing specialist
items.summary: A $20.6M (net of cash) deal gives founders a price comparison for small photonics test-tool companies and shows who is buying.

items.headline: Quantum Computing Inc. agrees to acquire Luminar Semiconductor
items.summary: Shows quantum and photonics companies buying in-house semiconductor laser and photonics capability.

items.headline: Dispelix and AAC Technologies partner to commercialize AR waveguides globally
items.summary: A waveguide maker teaming with a large device supplier means more supply competition, and possible partners or rivals, for AR optics startups.

items.headline: Federal Circuit finds lower court misread 'transparency' in '930 patent
items.summary: How a court defines a single claim word in an optics patent can decide the whole case.

items.headline: STMicroelectronics and Metalenz sign new metasurface optics license
items.summary: A major manufacturer now makes licensed flat-lens optics at volume, which founders can buy rather than build, and the licensor holding the patents is active.

items.headline: Arbitrators set royalties for InterDigital's patent license with Samsung
items.summary: Royalties set by arbitration give a reference point for what cellular and wireless patent licenses cost.

items.headline: Ericsson's lawsuits in several countries lead to a licensing win
items.summary: The article ties Ericsson's licensing win to lawsuits in several countries and also notes the Federal Circuit made anti-suit injunctions possible again, which shapes how disputes over standard-essential wireless patents get resolved.

items.headline: Federal Circuit vacates $300M Optis cellular patent verdict against Apple
items.summary: Large cellular patent verdicts can be overturned on appeal, which changes how founders should weigh lawsuit risk and negotiating leverage.

items.headline: Jury awards Headwater about $278M against Samsung in wireless patent trial
items.summary: A large Eastern-district-style jury award against a major phone maker shows how much money wireless patents held by non-practicing companies can bring in, so founders should look at who owns patents before launching device features.

items.headline: InterDigital licenses Wi-Fi and video patents to HP for PCs
items.summary: Wi-Fi patent licensing is spreading beyond phones to PCs, so founders building hardware with Wi-Fi should plan for royalty costs.

items.headline: Qualcomm renews global patent license agreement with Apple
items.summary: The renewal keeps a major hardware-platform licensing relationship stable from April 2027, which affects founders building on Apple devices.

items.headline: Google completes acquisition of cloud security platform Wiz
items.summary: Google closed its largest-ever acquisition, which shows big buyers will pay for cloud and AI security software startups.

items.headline: USPTO Desjardins precedent makes ML training claims potentially patent eligible
items.summary: AI founders now have a USPTO precedent, added to the MPEP, for arguing that claims improving how models are trained are eligible under §101.

items.headline: Federal Circuit vacates $300M Optis verdict against Apple
items.summary: Large patent verdicts can be overturned on §101 and claim-construction errors, which matters when weighing litigation risk and settlement leverage.

items.headline: Federal Circuit invalidates generic machine-learning patents in Recentive v. Fox
items.summary: Patent claims that only apply generic ML to a new field are at risk under §101, so founders should claim specific technical improvements.

items.headline: Federal Circuit affirms PTAB unpatentability of UPL fungicide-combination patent
items.summary: A combination patent in the dithiocarbamate/SDHI/EBI-QoI space was found unpatentable, which changes the patent picture for founders working on multi-active fungicide mixtures (other patents may still apply).
items.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit

items.headline: Biocontrol Technologies signs US distribution deal with Wilbur-Ellis for T34
items.summary: An example of a non-US biocontrol company entering the US market through an established distributor instead of building its own sales channel.

items.headline: Supreme Court rules 7-2 for Monsanto in Durnell Roundup FIFRA case
items.summary: The ruling on how FIFRA relates to state failure-to-warn claims affects how much product-label liability a pesticide founder may face.

items.headline: Biotalys and 21st.BIO partner to scale protein-based biocontrol production
items.summary: Shows that precision-fermentation partners are one route for biocontrol startups to get past manufacturing-scale bottlenecks.

items.headline: U.S. issues new suspension orders to five offshore wind projects
items.summary: Federal suspensions across several big U.S. offshore projects put near-term demand for offshore turbine technology at risk.

items.headline: TPG/MAVCO complete Siemens Gamesa India and Sri Lanka wind buy, form Vayona Energy
items.summary: A new privately owned turbine maker in India changes who founders sell to and partner with in that market.

items.headline: BOEM orders work on Revolution Wind offshore project to stop
items.summary: Federal orders to stop work make U.S. offshore wind demand less certain for startups selling turbine technology.

items.headline: Daikin America and Claros Technologies partner on PFAS destruction
items.summary: A large chemical maker teaming up with a startup on UV-based PFAS destruction is a sign of strategic interest in the area.

items.headline: EPA moves to formally rescind four PFAS drinking water limits
items.summary: Utilities must still meet the PFOA and PFOS limits but no longer the PFHxS, PFNA, PFBS and GenX ones, so treatment specs may shift.

items.headline: Photocat licenses photocatalytic water-treatment technology to Danish company
items.summary: Shows a licensing route where the licensee takes over commercial rollout of the technology.

items.headline: 374Water and Crystal Clean partner on PFAS waste destruction
items.summary: Pairs a destruction technology with a waste-collection network, a model founders could copy to reach customers.

items.headline: EPA announces plan to rescind several PFAS drinking water limits
items.summary: Fewer regulated PFAS and a 2031 deadline for PFOA/PFOS change the size and timing of the market for PFAS-removal products.

items.headline: Stratasys wins $27.6M patent verdict against Bambu Lab entities
items.summary: A large US damages award over desktop printer technology shows that patents on fused-filament printing can be costly to ignore, so founders building these printers should check freedom to operate early.

items.headline: Continuous Composites returns to court over continuous-fiber 3D printing patents
items.summary: Patents on continuous-fiber composite printing are being actively enforced, even against companies that had already signed a license.

items.headline: EOS acquires metal powder specialist Metalpine
items.summary: Printer makers are buying up their material suppliers, so founders who depend on outside metal powders may face more tightly controlled supply chains.

items.headline: UPC Hague denies Stratasys interim injunction against Bambu Lab
items.summary: The same patent dispute can end differently in the US and in Europe, which matters for founders deciding where to launch first.

items.headline: 3D Systems sells Oqton and 3DXpert software to Hubb Global Holdings
items.summary: Large printer makers are selling off their manufacturing-software units, which could open partnership or competition opportunities for software startups.
